title: Prefill priority fairness + kernel-adaptive smoothing for continuous batching
creator: Ava Park
description: Problem summary: As traffic patterns diversify (mix of short chat turns and long completion requests), our continuous batching admission currently favors throughput at the expense of tail latency and per-request fairness. Prefill-heavy requests can monopolize kernel budget, and occasional large kernels (long seq lengths or attention patterns) create jitter that violates customer P95 SLOs. This ticket designs and implements a two-part system: (1) a prefill priority fairness layer that enforces short-request reservations and weighted admission to reduce starvation, and (2) a kernel-adaptive smoothing controller that dynamically adjusts batch shaping and kernel selection windows to reduce tail spikes while keeping high GPU utilization.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end bench: P95 latency reduction >= 25% for mixed workload compared to baseline (same model/runtime) measured on dedicated cluster emulation
No regression > 5% in median throughput for steady-state workloads after feature enabled
Can be toggled per-tenant via feature flag and exposes two knobs: short-request reservation percent and kernel-smoothing aggressiveness
Unit + integration tests for admission logic, fairness counters, and kernel smoothing algorithm added to runtime test harness
Design doc and rollout playbook reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads
Observable metrics surfaced: admission_rejects_by_reason, reservation_utilization, kernel_switch_count, batch_shape_histogram, p50/p95/p99 latencies per model
design_notes:
High-level approach:

1) Prefill priority fairness layer
   - Maintain a lightweight short-request reservation pool: a small fraction (configurable, default 12%) of slot capacity is reserved for requests with prefill token length <= N (configurable, default 32 tokens). Reserved slots are exclusively for arriving short requests for a short window (30-100ms) to avoid head-of-line blocking.
   - Weighted admission: remaining capacity is admitted with weights proportional to recent fairness scores (EWMA-based) to avoid long-running tenants repeatedly bumping short requests. Fairness score per tenant is computed on a sliding window of admitted token-time.
   - Backpressure signals: when reservation saturation is observed, emit soft-shed metrics and route eligible requests to a faster kernel variant (quantized/short-seq optimized) when available.

2) Kernel-adaptive smoothing controller
   - Observe recent kernel execution latency distributions (per-device, per-model) and predict near-term kernel cost using a small feed-forward estimator (lightweight linear model) using features: input_length, requested_decode_length, attention_pattern (sparse/dense heuristics), KV-cache hit ratio, current batch size.
   - Use predictions to adjust admission: if the predicted kernel cost for an incoming request would push batch kernel tail over threshold, delay admission (micro-sleep up to 20ms) and attempt merging with next window. For long heavy kernels, proactively reduce batching window for those requests to avoid causing >P95 spikes.
   - Smoothing policy uses exponential backoff per-device to avoid oscillations; incorporate minimum admission window and max delay guardrails.

Trade-offs considered:
 - Reservation fraction hurts worst-case throughput; chosen default small to balance fairness vs utilization.
 - Predictive delaying can increase median latency for some long requests; but reduces tail for mixed workloads as measured in local benchmarks.
 - We avoid complex per-tenant ML in first iteration; use lightweight estimator and configurable policies to be operationally safe.

APIs/Config:
 - runtime config: short_reservation_percent (float), short_token_threshold (int), kernel_smooth_aggressiveness (enum low/med/high), max_admission_delay_ms (int), enable_weighted_admission (bool)
 - Console: per-tenant toggle + real-time reservation utilization visualization

Security/Privacy: No customer payloads are persisted. Only aggregated metrics and non-sensitive admission traces are emitted.

Open questions:
 - Best default for short_token_threshold across chat vs completion workloads (we will A/B with 16/32/64).
 - Whether to expose kernel prediction logits in observability for debugging (privacy vs debuggability).

testing_plan:
1) Local dev cluster: synthetic workload generator (shape mixture 70% short chat 30% long completion) to validate logic and run microbench iterations.
2) Performance harness: dedicated infra tests to measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput vs baseline (runtime vX). Use multiple seeds and traffic mixes; run each config for 30 minutes to observe steady-state.
3) Canary: enable on small set of Dedicated nodes (5% traffic) with tight monitoring for latency regressions. Use canary to tune short_token_threshold and reservation percent.
4) Chaos tests: inject slow kernel execution and device noise to ensure backoff and smoothing avoid oscillations.
5) Regression tests: ensure feature off path matches current production behavior.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Dev+QA): feature branch, unit/integration tests, and perf reports (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (Canary): enable for 5% of Dedicated capacity for 48 hours; monitor P95/P99 and reservation_utilization. If P95 improves and throughput within expected range, proceed.
Phase 3 (Gradual rollout): ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2–4 days each with automated checks.
Rollback triggers: >20% regression in p95 or >10% sustained drop in throughput or significant increase in error/retry rates.
monitoring_alerts: admission_delay_spikes where 95th percentile delay > configured max_admission_delay_ms
